source.locator: example 2.1 (the areal daily precipitation maxima of a catchment, N = 30): table 2.1, pp. 20-21, eqs. 2.13 to 2.15, p. 21 (epsilon = 19.6 mm, mu = 3.355, sigma = 0.677), eq. 2.9, p. 19, step 7, eq. 2.19 and table 2.3, p. 24 (P_max,p and the upper bound P^84%_max,p at p = 50 %)

intermediate_rounding.step: sigma printed 0.677 (eq. 2.15) and P_max,p printed 48.24 (table 2.3), which KZGW computed and used unrounded (sigma = 0.677347 by eqs. 2.4 to 2.6 from table 2.1): the largest change of the bound over the four corners sigma +- 0.0005, P_max,p +- 0.005, evaluated through the conversion shape = sigma, loc = 0, scale = P_max,p exp(-sigma u_p), under which the bound is P_max,p exp(z sigma / sqrt(N) sqrt(1 + u_p**2 / 2)); these inputs are therefore not in printed_precision, whose corners the reference module would take in scipy's parameters
u_beta = 0.994 for beta = 84 % (step 7a) against z = Phi^-1(0.84) = 0.994458: the bound times exp((z - 0.994) sigma / sqrt(N) sqrt(1 + u_p**2 / 2)) - 1, at the upper corner

conventions: the upper bound of KZGW's one-sided beta = 84 % interval is the upper bound of the central two-sided interval at c = 2 beta - 1 = 0.68: confidence_levels [0.68], expected the row upper

the delta method on the scale of ln(x - loc) with the expected information of the normal mean and standard deviation, the interval Q_p exp(+- u sigma / sqrt(N) sqrt(1 + u_p**2 / 2)) of the two-parameter log-normal (eq. 2.9; Stedinger et al. 1993, eq. 18.4.8), u_p = Phi^-1(1 - p)
p of the table is the exceedance probability, T = 100 / p = 2 years
the closed form uses the sample only through N: values are the 30 areal daily maxima P_max of table 2.1 [mm], 1984-2013, chronological, whose printed digits do not enter
sigma is KZGW's printed estimate, given as the shape: KZGW's eq. 2.6 (2.15) divides by N - 1 where Hydrolog's maximum-likelihood s divides by N, which changes what a fit would give, not this case

KZGW's fit is the three-parameter log-normal, its bound epsilon = 19.6 mm by eq. 2.4 (2.13) from the sample's extremes and median, and eq. 2.9 multiplies the whole quantile, epsilon included; Hydrolog holds the bound of the support (loc, 0 in its own fits) and multiplies Q_p - loc, so the case gives loc = 0 and the scale of a two-parameter log-normal through the printed P_max,p = 48.24, scale = P_max,p exp(-sigma u_p): Hydrolog's quantile is then the printed one and its bound eq. 2.9 as KZGW evaluates it, one return period per case since each quantile needs its own scale; with loc = epsilon Hydrolog would give epsilon + (P_max,p - epsilon) exp(...), below KZGW's bound by epsilon (exp(...) - 1)
a precipitation depth is never below 0: variable discharge, whose sign rule it shares

eq. 2.19 prints u_p = 1.282 and 103.71 mm at p = 10 %; table 2.3 follows from the unrounded u_p, sigma and P_max,p (all six of its bounds are reproduced from eqs. 2.4 to 2.6 on table 2.1 with u_beta = 0.994)
